steps.title: Screen graph: the recorder creates the source node of a recorded action when missing (from the before fingerprint), so the launch screen enters the graph without a prior describe; MULTIHOP non-inferiority uses the pre-registered strict form (lo > -5)

verify.cmd: cd packages/tool-server && npx vitest run test/screen-graph-*.test.ts --maxWorkers=2

steps.commitMessage: fix(screen-graph): record the launch screen as the source of the first action

verifyRuns.cmd: cd packages/tool-server && npx vitest run test/screen-graph-*.test.ts --maxWorkers=2

findings.note: L413+L448: a cross-app action (launcher icon -> app, or back from app root -> launcher) now persists a FOREIGN source node and its edge in the destination app's store (store picked by post-action info.currentPackage at L318); before this step the dangling edge was swept on flush. The launcher's compact (installed app names) lands on disk under the app's graph dir and the node is dead weight (navigate-to never plans from it: the store is resolved by the current package). Fix: only mint the source when the before tree belongs to pkg (resourceId prefix `pkg:id/` majority on opts.beforeTree), and for tree-less actions skip minting (old sweep behavior); add a test with a launcher-package before tree.
findings.cause: The source package is never checked: OpenServerActionOutcome.before has no package, and the store is chosen from the AFTER getInfo, so the source of a cross-app action is attributed to the destination app.

findings.note: L101-108: a source minted from the before tree has a title-only label ('Settings', not 'Settings: Settings') and no stateHash; the summary tier only re-renders !known or bare nodes, and the recorder's revisit branch only refreshes structuralHash, so the label stays title-only until a compact describe. navigate-to {label:'Settings: Settings'} (the documented Activity: title form, features/screen-graph.mdx L37-38) finds nothing, and label:'Settings' now full-matches this node instead of failing closed on two title-half matches. Fix: in the summary tier also renderFresh when the known node is not redacted/template and has stateHash === undefined (recorder-minted; the tree is already in hand, no extra RPC).
findings.cause: The recorder has no activity for the before screen (getInfo is post-action), and nothing on the summary path upgrades a recorder-minted node to a describe-built one.

findings.note: L413: ensureSourceNode(store, beforeId, sourceScreen()) evaluates sourceScreen() eagerly, so EVERY templated tap rebuilds compact+index of the whole before tree (formatDescribeTree) even when the source is already a node and the result is discarded. Fix: `if (!store.hasNode(beforeId)) ensureSourceNode(store, beforeId, sourceScreen());`. The template-path minting is also untested (the e2e test runs with ARGENT_SG_TEMPLATES unset); add one case with templates on.
findings.cause: Argument evaluated before ensureSourceNode's own hasNode short-circuit; the lazy fetchBeforeScreen used in the recordObservation path was not applied to the template path.

findings.note: L340-359: the before tree and outcome.before.idHash are two reads; on the launch screen (splash -> main, the case this step targets) the tree can be of a different frame than the idHash, and the node keeps that compact/index/label because the summary tier never re-renders a non-bare node. The comment drops stateHash so only the COMPACT tier refreshes. Fix: compare a host-side structural hash of opts.beforeTree with outcome.before.hash and mint bare on a mismatch (the bare node is rendered fresh by tiered.ts); or rely on the stateHash===undefined refresh from the tiered.ts finding.
findings.cause: The tree/fingerprint pairing is not checked, and the mitigation only covers the compact tier.

findings.note: L104-115: a self-edge with no secret and no fetchScreen mints the source (visits 1) and then the target branch bumps it again (visits 2), so this caller shape counts one action as two visits. The wiring always passes fetchScreen, so this is not reachable today. Fix: set targetMintsSource = before.hash === after.hash (the target branch handles a known node with one visit), or document the caller contract.

L14: 'Bench: MULTIHOP rep 0 no longer fails' cannot be verified from the diff. The unit and e2e tests cover the mechanism (6 of the new tests fail when run against the HEAD versions of recorder.ts, wiring and tiered.ts). Still to check: a MULTIHOP run (bench-screen-graph.yml, emulator_build=15004761 pinned) where the 3 graph-arm failures at rep 0 are gone and the strict lo > -5 holds.

steps.commitMessage: fix(ios-sim-input): ease-out release so a momentum-free swipe does not fling

verifyRuns.cmd: cd packages/tool-server && npx vitest run test/ios-sim-input-service.test.ts test/ios-sim-input-blueprint.test.ts --maxWorkers=2

findings.note: L405: the simInputMomentumFreeEnabled doc still gives the old gate ('offset equal to OFF's within the IQR'). The plan amendment (item 3) and the README L118-120 say 'within 10 % of OFF's median (344.7 pt), IQR <= 15 % of the median'. Reword the comment to the amended gate

L131-133/L88-97: at durationMs 150 the ease-out plan has 1 constant frame, so the first 16 ms move jumps 146 pt (9104 pt/s, 7456 pt/s on frame 2). The linear plan moved 43.7 pt per 12 ms (~3640 pt/s). A single jump far past the touch slop can change how UIScrollView's pan recognizer starts (translation baseline, lost slop), and so the scroll offset. Not checkable from the diff: check it in measure-deferred with one 150 ms ON-siminput bench arm, or cap the peak by letting short swipes shorten the tail

L118-127: the release physics are not checkable from the diff. The selftest pins only planned positions (last 3 frames 4.0/6.3/14.7 pt/s). The last 6 frames still run 64/101/236 pt/s, and the hold is 116 ms, not 120 (first dwell pulse on the last move's deadline, Support.swift L147). Promotion stays behind ARGENT_SIM_INPUT_MOMENTUM_FREE until the measure-deferred bench gives the ON-siminput optical offset at 250 ms against OFF 344.7 pt +/- 10 %, IQR <= 15 %
